_schema.description: Structured bibliography for Checkpoint 1. Single source of truth: references.bib and literature_matrix.csv are generated from this file by scripts/build_bib.py.

verification_levels.V-DOI: Title, authors, venue, year, and DOI seen together in at least one publisher, repository, or indexing record returned by web search on 2026-11-02.
verification_levels.V-META: Title, authors, venue, and year verified; DOI not seen in any retrieved record (left blank on purpose, never guessed).
verification_levels.V-PRE: Exists as a preprint (arXiv or similar); no peer-reviewed version confirmed.
verification_levels.PARTIAL: Exists, but at least one metadata field conflicts across sources or could not be confirmed (noted in 'notes').
verification_levels.UNVERIFIED: Surfaced once in a search snippet; existence or content not independently confirmed. Do not cite until checked.

_schema.review_depth: All entries were reviewed at the abstract and metadata level through search-engine snippets and repository pages. No full text was read: arxiv.org, doi.org, api.crossref.org, and publisher sites were blocked by this session's network policy. Limitations marked [A] come from the authors' own statements; those marked [I] are our inference and must be confirmed against the full text.

entries.authors: Samarakoon, S. and Siriwardhana, Y. and Porambage, P. and Liyanage, M. and Chang, S.-Y. and Kim, J. and Kim, J. and Ylianttila, M.
entries.title: 5G-NIDD: A Comprehensive Network Intrusion Detection Dataset Generated over 5G Wireless Network
entries.problem: There was no labelled intrusion dataset captured on a real 5G network.
entries.contribution: Labelled flow and packet dataset from the Oulu 5G Test Network: 9 classes (benign plus DoS floods and port scans), 2 base stations.
entries.method: Attack generation on a live 5G testbed; CICFlowMeter-style flow features.
entries.env: University of Oulu 5GTN, real 5G NSA/SA infrastructure.
entries.findings: Reported baseline ML classifiers reach very high accuracy.
entries.limitations: [I] Volumetric and scan attacks only; 2 capture days, so temporal diversity is limited; no slice labels; random-split baselines are probably optimistic (see the tvquynh reproducibility package).
entries.relevance: Primary trace source for detector scores and benign-flow statistics in the replay arm of the evaluation.
entries.notes: Superseded by the 2025 IEEE Data Descriptions descriptor (siriwardhana2025nidd).

entries.authors: Siriwardhana, Y. and Samarakoon, S. and Porambage, P. and Liyanage, M. and Chang, S.-Y. and Kim, J. and Kim, J. and Ylianttila, M.
entries.title: Descriptor: 5G Wireless Network Intrusion Detection Dataset (5G-NIDD)
entries.contribution: Formal dataset description; DataPort DOI 10.21227/xtep-hv36.
entries.relevance: Canonical citation for 5G-NIDD.
entries.notes: The first author differs between the preprint and the descriptor.

entries.authors: Khan, M. S. and Farzaneh, B. and Shahriar, N. and Saha, N. and Boutaba, R.
entries.title: SliceSecure: Impact and Detection of DoS/DDoS Attacks on 5G Network Slices
entries.problem: How DoS/DDoS affects individual slices, and how to detect it per slice.
entries.contribution: Slice-level attack dataset (DataPort 10.21227/32k1-dr12) and a BiLSTM detector.
entries.findings: [A] 99.99% detection accuracy on their dataset; shows the bandwidth and latency impact on slice users.
entries.limitations: [I] Detection only, with no response policy; near-perfect accuracy on a self-generated dataset suggests an easy or leaky split; collateral impact of any mitigation is not measured.
entries.relevance: Closest slice-security work. Shows that attacks degrade slice SLAs, but stops at detection, which is the gap the primary candidate targets.
entries.notes: Year inferred from the ResearchGate listing (369099482); venue unconfirmed.

entries.authors: Farzaneh, B. and others
entries.title: DTL-5G: Deep Transfer Learning-based DDoS Attack Detection in 5G and Beyond Networks
entries.problem: DDoS detection in a new 5G domain with few labels.
entries.contribution: Transfer-learning detector.
entries.relevance: Cross-domain detection baseline.
entries.notes: Full author list, year, and volume not verified; the venue is inferred from the file name 'COMCOM'.

entries.authors: Amponis, G. and others
entries.title: Threatening the 5G Core via PFCP DoS Attacks: The Case of Blocking UAV Communications
entries.venue: EURASIP Journal on Wireless Communications and Networking
entries.problem: Control-plane (N4/PFCP) DoS between SMF and UPF.
entries.contribution: PFCP attack emulation and the 5GC PFCP intrusion dataset.
entries.method: Scapy-crafted PFCP session establishment, deletion, and modification attacks; CICFlowMeter plus PFCP flow features.
entries.findings: [A] Unauthorised PFCP messages can disrupt tunnels without breaking RAN connectivity.
entries.limitations: [A/I] One DataPort comment questions the agreement between labels and PCAPs; the attack set is narrow.
entries.relevance: Second trace source, for control-plane attacks.
entries.notes: The DOI was taken from the publisher URL pattern; the full author list was not retrieved.

entries.authors: Manca, C. and Scano, C. and Piras, G. and Brau, F. and Pintor, M. and Biggio, B.
entries.title: SAGE-5GC: Security-Aware Guidelines for Evaluating Anomaly Detection in the 5G Core Network
entries.problem: Anomaly-detector evaluation in the 5GC ignores adaptive adversaries.
entries.contribution: Evaluation guidelines; adversarially crafted PFCP attacks.
entries.method: Several anomaly detectors plus adversarial manipulation.
entries.relevance: Threat to candidate C10; adversarial-robustness baseline protocol.

entries.authors: (not retrieved)
entries.title: Slice-Aware Spoofing Detection in 5G Networks Using Lightweight Machine Learning
entries.contribution: Per-slice lightweight ML models.
entries.relevance: Shows that slice stratification of detectors has been done; the primary contribution therefore cannot be 'per-slice detection' alone.
entries.notes: Authors not retrieved.

entries.authors: (not retrieved)
entries.title: A Rogue gNodeB's Manipulation of 5G Network Slice ...
entries.problem: Slice manipulation by a rogue gNB.
entries.contribution: Per-slice-UPF Open5GS testbed with released Docker scripts (github.com/jxu96/Open5GS-Docker).
entries.env: Open5GS with per-slice UPF and per-slice rate/latency shaping.
entries.relevance: Reusable open-source scaffolding for an emulated sliced-core testbed.
entries.notes: The title is truncated in the search result; authors not retrieved.

entries.authors: Sommer, R. and Paxson, V.
entries.title: Outside the Closed World: On Using Machine Learning for Network Intrusion Detection
entries.venue: IEEE Symposium on Security and Privacy
entries.problem: Why ML-based NIDS rarely work operationally.
entries.contribution: Analysis of the mismatch between NIDS and other ML domains: high cost of errors, the semantic gap, and evaluation difficulty.
entries.findings: [A] The cost of false positives is a central obstacle.
entries.relevance: Foundational argument that operational cost of errors, not accuracy, should drive design. The primary candidate formalises that cost per slice.

entries.authors: Arp, D. and Quiring, E. and Pendlebury, F. and Warnecke, A. and Pierazzi, F. and Wressnegger, C. and Cavallaro, L. and Rieck, K.
entries.title: Dos and Don'ts of Machine Learning in Computer Security
entries.contribution: Ten pitfalls with recommendations; a review of 30 papers.
entries.findings: [A] The pitfalls are widespread and inflate results.
entries.relevance: Checklist for the evaluation protocol (sampling bias, data snooping, base-rate fallacy).
entries.notes: USENIX papers have no DOI.

entries.authors: Pendlebury, F. and Pierazzi, F. and Jordaney, R. and Kinder, J. and Cavallaro, L.
entries.title: TESSERACT: Eliminating Experimental Bias in Malware Classification across Space and Time
entries.problem: Spatial and temporal bias in evaluation.
entries.contribution: Space and time constraints and an AUT robustness metric.
entries.relevance: Motivates the temporally ordered calibration and test splits.

entries.authors: Engelen, G. and Rimmer, V. and Joosen, W.
entries.title: Troubleshooting an Intrusion Detection Dataset: the CICIDS2017 Case Study
entries.problem: Labelling and feature-extraction flaws in CICIDS2017.
entries.contribution: Corrected dataset and extractor; more than 20% of traces relabelled.
entries.relevance: Precedent for the dataset audit required in Phase 3.

entries.authors: Flood, R. and Engelen, G. and Aspinall, D. and Desmet, L.
entries.title: Bad Design Smells in Benchmark NIDS Datasets
entries.venue: IEEE European Symposium on Security and Privacy (EuroS\&P)
entries.problem: Systematic design flaws in seven benchmark NIDS datasets.
entries.contribution: Six 'data design smells' and heuristics to measure them; Distinguished Paper award.
entries.findings: [A] The smells cause severe experimental bias.
entries.relevance: Audit heuristics to apply to 5G-NIDD and the testbed data.
entries.notes: IEEE Xplore document 10629000 appeared next to this record but was not confirmed to be the same paper.

entries.authors: Apruzzese, G. and Laskov, P. and Schneider, J.
entries.title: SoK: Pragmatic Assessment of Machine Learning for Network Intrusion Detection
entries.venue: IEEE European Symposium on Security and Privacy (EuroS\&P)
entries.problem: The gap between research evaluation and operational assessment.
entries.contribution: Pragmatic assessment methodology.
entries.relevance: Supports cost-aware, operational metrics.
entries.notes: The EuroS&P DOI was not retrieved.

entries.authors: Jacobs, A. S. and Beltiukov, R. and Willinger, W. and Ferreira, R. A. and Gupta, A. and Granville, L. Z.
entries.title: AI/ML for Network Security: The Emperor has no Clothes
entries.venue: ACM SIGSAC Conference on Computer and Communications Security (CCS)
entries.problem: ML NIDS learn shortcuts and are underspecified.
entries.contribution: Trustee explanation framework exposing shortcut learning.
entries.findings: [A] Best Paper Honorable Mention; models rely on spurious features.
entries.limitations: [I] Explains models; does not decide actions.
entries.relevance: Motivates shift-robust calibration rather than trusting raw scores.
entries.notes: DOI not retrieved.

entries.authors: Layeghy, S. and Portmann, M.
entries.title: Explainable Cross-Domain Evaluation of ML-based Network Intrusion Detection Systems
entries.problem: NIDS that look good in-domain fail across datasets.
entries.contribution: Cross-dataset evaluation with an explanation of feature-importance shift.
entries.method: Train on one dataset, test on another; SHAP.
entries.relevance: Evidence that calibration fitted on one domain will not transfer, which motivates the shift-robustness work package.
entries.notes: The author list differs between UQ and DBLP.

entries.authors: Sarhan, M. and Layeghy, S. and Portmann, M.
entries.title: Towards a Standard Feature Set for Network Intrusion Detection System Datasets
entries.problem: Incompatible feature sets across NIDS datasets.
entries.contribution: NetFlow-based standard feature sets (12 and 43 features); the NF-* datasets.
entries.findings: [A] Comparable or better detection on NetFlow features.
entries.relevance: Shared feature space for 5G-NIDD and testbed captures.
entries.notes: The DOI was shown on the arXiv listing; the publisher page was not reached.

entries.authors: Mirsky, Y. and Doitshman, T. and Elovici, Y. and Shabtai, A.
entries.title: Kitsune: An Ensemble of Autoencoders for Online Network Intrusion Detection
entries.venue: Network and Distributed System Security Symposium (NDSS)
entries.contribution: KitNET autoencoder ensemble.
entries.method: Incremental feature extraction plus an autoencoder ensemble.
entries.env: IP-camera and IoT networks; Raspberry Pi.
entries.limitations: [I] Threshold chosen heuristically; no error-rate guarantee.
entries.relevance: Unsupervised score-producing detector, usable as an input to the response layer.

entries.authors: Yang, L. and Guo, W. and Hao, Q. and Ciptadi, A. and Ahmadzadeh, A. and Xing, X. and Wang, G.
entries.title: CADE: Detecting and Explaining Concept Drift Samples for Security Applications
entries.problem: Flag drifting samples one at a time.
entries.contribution: Contrastive autoencoder plus distance-based explanation.
entries.limitations: [I] No action layer; no coverage guarantee.
entries.relevance: Drift-detection baseline for the shift monitor.

entries.authors: Han, D. and others
entries.title: Anomaly Detection in the Open World: Normality Shift Detection, Explanation, and Adaptation
entries.venue: Network and Distributed System Security Symposium (NDSS)
entries.problem: Shifts in benign behaviour break zero-positive anomaly detectors.
entries.contribution: OWAD: detection, explanation, and adaptation of normality shift.
entries.relevance: Benign-traffic shift is exactly what breaks collateral-risk calibration. OWAD is a candidate shift detector for triggering recalibration.
entries.notes: The DOI is inferred from the proceedings identifier 'ndss.2023.24830' seen in the listing; confirm it.

entries.authors: Barbero, F. and Pendlebury, F. and Pierazzi, F. and Cavallaro, L.
entries.title: Transcending Transcend: Revisiting Malware Classification in the Presence of Concept Drift
entries.venue: IEEE Symposium on Security and Privacy (S\&P)
entries.problem: Rejecting drifting samples using conformal evaluation.
entries.contribution: TRANSCENDENT: formal treatment and new conformal evaluators.
entries.method: Conformal p-values, credibility and confidence thresholds.
entries.findings: [A] Matches or beats Transcend at lower cost.
entries.limitations: [I] Classification with reject only; no network actions; no per-group risk control.
entries.relevance: Foundational conformal-security prior work; threat for C2.

entries.authors: Barrett, S. and Li, L. and Dorai, G. and Rajaganapathy, S.
entries.title: FIRCE: A Framework for Intrusion Response and Conformal Evaluation
entries.contribution: Four conformal evaluators (including an approximate cross-conformal one) plus adaptive chunking that triggers retraining.
entries.method: Conformal evaluation for drift detection; retraining as the 'response'.
entries.findings: [A] Efficient, robust response to changing threats.
entries.limitations: [I] 'Response' means model retraining, not network mitigation; no collateral-damage risk bound.
entries.relevance: MAJOR THREAT to the naming and framing of the primary candidate. Must be differentiated explicitly.
entries.notes: Venue taken from search-result text; confirm it.

entries.authors: Youssef, M. A.
entries.title: CALIBURN: Operationally Calibrated Streaming Intrusion Detection with Regime-Dependent Conformal Risk Control
entries.problem: Alert thresholds under a false-positive budget in streaming NIDS.
entries.contribution: Bayesian online change-point detection, isotonic calibration, and regime-dependent CRC; burn-rate alerting.
entries.findings: Not verified. A third party reports AUC-PR 0.943, which is unconfirmed.
entries.limitations: [A] 'Not a universal replacement'. [I] Controls an alert-level FP budget, not the service-level impact of actions.
entries.relevance: MAJOR THREAT to C2; closest prior work for the risk-control mechanism in C1.
entries.notes: The arXiv PDF for the same ID is titled 'Stream Assembly Is an Uncontrolled Treatment in Streaming Intrusion-Detection Benchmarks', so the paper was likely retitled. Resolve which version is current.

entries.authors: (not retrieved)
entries.title: Robust Conformal Intrusion Detection via Traffic-Aware Calibration and Attack-Orbit Invariance
entries.problem: Conformal coverage under adversarial test-time perturbations.
entries.contribution: An orbit-invariance condition under which a clean calibration threshold remains valid.
entries.findings: [A] The score-inflation gap is zero for orbit-invariant procedures.
entries.relevance: Threat to C2; possible tool for an adversarial-robustness extension of C1.
entries.notes: Authors not retrieved.

entries.authors: (not retrieved)
entries.title: ConFID: A Conformal One-Class Framework for Unsupervised Zero-Day Intrusion Detection in IoT Networks
entries.problem: FPR control for zero-day IoT intrusion detection.
entries.contribution: One-class detector with conformal FPR at most alpha under exchangeability.
entries.relevance: Threat to C2: marginal FPR control for IDS already exists.
entries.notes: The journal is inferred from the ScienceDirect PII prefix; authors not retrieved.

entries.authors: Farzaneh, A. and Simeone, O.
entries.title: Context-Aware Online Conformal Anomaly Detection with Prediction-Powered Data Acquisition
entries.problem: Online conformal anomaly detection with scarce labels.
entries.contribution: Controls a smoothed, decaying false-discovery rate; prediction-powered data acquisition.
entries.method: Online conformal p-values plus synthetic calibration data.
entries.limitations: [I] Controls detection FDR, not action consequences.
entries.relevance: Threat to C2.
entries.notes: One search snippet said it was evaluated on 5G-NIDD; another could not confirm this. Unresolved.

entries.authors: (not retrieved)
entries.title: CALM-5G: Event-Level Conformal Risk Control for Predictive Service-Assurance Alarms
entries.problem: Miss-rate control for predictive service-assurance alarms.
entries.contribution: Event-level CRC.
entries.relevance: Potential threat: CRC already applied to 5G alarms, though for faults rather than security and alarms rather than actions.
entries.notes: Seen in one search snippet; a direct search did not find it. Do not cite until resolved.

entries.authors: (not retrieved)
entries.title: Risk-Calibrated Bayesian Streaming Intrusion Detection with SRE-Aligned Decisions
entries.contribution: Bayesian risk-calibrated detector with SRE-style decisions.
entries.limitations: [I] Bayesian calibration, not distribution-free; no slice structure.
entries.relevance: Threat to C1 at the decision layer; must be read in full.

entries.authors: Cohen, K. M. and Park, S. and Simeone, O. and Shamai (Shitz), S.
entries.title: Calibrating AI Models for Wireless Communications via Conformal Prediction
entries.contribution: First application of CP to demodulation, modulation classification, and channel prediction.
entries.method: Split, cross, and validation-based CP; frequentist and Bayesian.
entries.relevance: Establishes CP in the communications community; not a threat to C1.
entries.notes: The IEEE TMLCN version and DOI were not confirmed.

entries.authors: Tibshirani, R. J. and Barber, R. F. and Cand{\`e}s, E. J. and Ramdas, A.
entries.title: Conformal Prediction Under Covariate Shift
entries.venue: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS)
entries.problem: CP validity when test covariates shift.
entries.contribution: Weighted CP using likelihood ratios.
entries.limitations: [A] Requires a known or estimated likelihood ratio.
entries.relevance: Tool for shift-robust collateral-risk certification.

entries.authors: Barber, R. F. and Cand{\`e}s, E. J. and Ramdas, A. and Tibshirani, R. J.
entries.title: Conformal Prediction Beyond Exchangeability
entries.contribution: Coverage-gap bound in terms of total-variation deviation, using fixed weights.
entries.findings: [A] Coverage degrades gracefully with mild deviation.
entries.limitations: [A] The bound depends on unknown TV terms.
entries.relevance: Template for the shift-degradation bound in C1.

entries.authors: Gibbs, I. and Cand{\`e}s, E. J.
entries.title: Adaptive Conformal Inference Under Distribution Shift
entries.venue: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS)
entries.contribution: ACI: online update of alpha.
entries.relevance: Online adaptation baseline for C1.
entries.notes: A JMLR 2024 extension exists (gibbs2024online).

entries.authors: Gibbs, I. and Cand{\`e}s, E. J.
entries.title: Conformal Inference for Online Prediction with Arbitrary Distribution Shifts
entries.contribution: Adaptive step sizes.
entries.relevance: Online variant for C1.
entries.notes: Volume and pages not retrieved.

entries.authors: Bates, S. and Cand{\`e}s, E. and Lei, L. and Romano, Y. and Sesia, M.
entries.title: Testing for Outliers with Conformal p-values
entries.contribution: Positive dependence implies FDR control; conditionally valid p-values.
entries.relevance: The theory behind conformal FPR control of detectors (C2), and therefore evidence that C2 is not novel.

entries.authors: Angelopoulos, A. N. and Bates, S. and Fisch, A. and Lei, L. and Schuster, T.
entries.title: Conformal Risk Control
entries.problem: Controlling the expected value of a monotone loss.
entries.contribution: CRC with O(1/n) tightness; extensions to shift and multiple risks.
entries.relevance: Collateral loss in C1 is NOT monotone in a multi-action policy, so plain CRC is insufficient and LTT is needed.

entries.authors: Angelopoulos, A. N. and Bates, S. and Cand{\`e}s, E. J. and Jordan, M. I. and Lei, L.
entries.title: Learn then Test: Calibrating Predictive Algorithms to Achieve Risk Control
entries.problem: Risk control for arbitrary, non-monotone, multiple risks.
entries.contribution: Risk control recast as multiple hypothesis testing (FWER).
entries.limitations: [A] Guarantee holds for i.i.d. calibration data; [I] conservative when there are many hypotheses.
entries.relevance: CORE statistical tool for C1.
entries.notes: Volume not retrieved.

entries.authors: (not retrieved)
entries.title: Conformal Risk Control for Non-Monotonic Losses
entries.contribution: Not verified.
entries.relevance: Alternative to LTT for C1; compare in Phase 2.

entries.authors: (not retrieved)
entries.title: CORA: Conformal Risk-Controlled Agents for Safeguarded Mobile GUI Automation
entries.problem: Bounding the rate of harmful autonomous actions.
entries.contribution: CRC on an action-execution threshold.
entries.limitations: [I] Single binary execute/defer decision; not networking.
entries.relevance: Methodological analogue for C1. It shows the mechanism 'risk-controlled action gating' exists, so C1 cannot claim the mechanism as new; the novelty must lie in the networking problem structure.

entries.authors: (not retrieved)
entries.title: Conformal Policy Control
entries.problem: Risk control when the control parameter is on the policy.
entries.contribution: Not verified in detail.
entries.relevance: Threat and tool for C1's multi-action policy calibration; must be read in full in Phase 1.

entries.authors: Tartakovsky, A. G. and Rozovskii, B. L. and Bla{\v{z}}ek, R. B. and Kim, H.
entries.title: A Novel Approach to Detection of Intrusions in Computer Networks via Adaptive Sequential and Batch-Sequential Change-Point Detection Methods
entries.contribution: Adaptive CUSUM-type and batch-sequential detectors with FAR control.
entries.findings: [A] Minimal delay at a given FAR.
entries.relevance: Foundation for backup candidate C3.
entries.notes: Author list as recalled; only 'Tartakovsky et al.' was confirmed. DOI not retrieved.

entries.authors: Fellouris, G. and Sokolov, G.
entries.title: Second-Order Asymptotic Optimality in Multisensor Sequential Change Detection
entries.problem: Multistream QCD with an unknown affected subset.
entries.contribution: Second-order optimality of generalised CUSUM rules.
entries.findings: [A] Bounded extra delay versus the oracle.
entries.relevance: Core theory threat for C3. C3 must add heterogeneous (SLA-weighted) delay costs and coupled streams to be novel.

entries.authors: shrirang73
entries.title: topic7-slice-anomaly: Quickest Detection of QoS Violations across 5G Network Slices (simulation)
entries.contribution: Simulation comparing per-stream versus multivariate CUSUM/MEWMA; cross-slice coherence analysis.
entries.findings: [A] The gain is governed by cross-slice coherence at frequency zero.
entries.limitations: [A] Not peer-reviewed; QoS faults, not attacks.
entries.relevance: Direct threat signal for C3. The idea is circulating, so publication pressure is high.
entries.notes: Not a peer-reviewed paper; listed for novelty-threat traceability only.

entries.authors: Hammar, K. and Stadler, R.
entries.title: Intrusion Prevention Through Optimal Stopping
entries.venue: IEEE Transactions on Network and Service Management
entries.contribution: POMDP and optimal-stopping formulation; threshold-structured optimal policies; the T-SPSA RL algorithm.
entries.limitations: [I] Model-based. Guarantees are relative to the POMDP model, not distribution-free on real collateral impact. Not slice-aware.
entries.relevance: STRONGEST methodological competitor for C1; mandatory baseline.

entries.authors: Hammar, K. and Stadler, R.
entries.title: Learning Near-Optimal Intrusion Responses Against Dynamic Attackers
entries.venue: IEEE Transactions on Network and Service Management
entries.contribution: Game-theoretic learning of response strategies.
entries.relevance: Baseline and threat for C1.
entries.notes: DOI not retrieved.

entries.authors: Hammar, K. and Stadler, R.
entries.title: Scalable Learning of Intrusion Response Through Recursive Decomposition
entries.venue: Decision and Game Theory for Security (GameSec)
entries.contribution: Recursive decomposition into subgames with threshold best responses.
entries.relevance: Threat for C1 (structure of threshold response policies).

entries.authors: Hammar, K. and Li, T. and Stadler, R. and Zhu, Q.
entries.title: Adaptive Security Response Strategies Through Conjectural Online Learning
entries.venue: IEEE Transactions on Information Forensics and Security
entries.problem: Online adaptation of response under model misspecification.
entries.contribution: Conjectural online learning.
entries.relevance: Threat for C1's shift-adaptive arm.
entries.notes: DOI not retrieved.

entries.authors: Zonouz, S. A. and Khurana, H. and Sanders, W. H. and Yardley, T. M.
entries.title: RRE: A Game-Theoretic Intrusion Response and Recovery Engine
entries.venue: IEEE Transactions on Parallel and Distributed Systems
entries.problem: Choosing response actions under alert uncertainty.
entries.contribution: Partially observable competitive MDP over attack-response trees.
entries.limitations: [I] Model-based costs; no statistical guarantee on collateral impact.
entries.relevance: Classical IRS baseline for C1.

entries.authors: (not retrieved)
entries.title: REGARD: Rules of EngaGement for Automated cybeR Defense to aid in Intrusion Response
entries.problem: Which response actions may be automated.
entries.contribution: Rules-of-engagement framework.
entries.relevance: Motivates the action-set design and human-in-the-loop fallback in C1.

entries.authors: Liu, Z. and Namkung, H. and Nikolaidis, G. and Lee, J. and Kim, C. and Jin, X. and Braverman, V. and Yu, M. and Sekar, V.
entries.title: Jaqen: A High-Performance Switch-Native Approach for Detecting and Mitigating Volumetric DDoS Attacks with Programmable Switches
entries.contribution: Switch-native detection and mitigation with universal sketches.
entries.findings: [A] Mitigates large hybrid attacks within seconds.
entries.limitations: [I] Not mobile-core or slice aware; collateral impact handled heuristically.
entries.relevance: Mitigation-primitive baseline for C1's action set.
entries.notes: Full title as recalled; the search confirmed authors, venue, and pages.

entries.authors: Foukas, X. and Patounas, G. and Elmokashfi, A. and Marina, M. K.
entries.title: Network Slicing in 5G: Survey and Challenges
entries.contribution: Survey and open questions.
entries.relevance: Background.
entries.notes: Survey (background only).

entries.authors: Foukas, X. and Marina, M. K. and Kontovasilis, K.
entries.title: Orion: RAN Slicing for a Flexible and Cost-Effective Multi-Service Mobile Network Architecture
entries.problem: Functional and performance isolation of RAN slices.
entries.contribution: RAN slicing system with on-the-fly base-station virtualisation.
entries.relevance: Isolation assumptions behind cross-slice collateral effects.

entries.authors: Afolabi, I. and Taleb, T. and Samdanis, K. and Ksentini, A. and Flinck, H.
entries.title: Network Slicing and Softwarization: A Survey on Principles, Enabling Technologies, and Solutions
entries.contribution: Survey.
entries.relevance: Background.
entries.notes: Survey (background only).

entries.authors: Bega, D. and Gramaglia, M. and Fiore, M. and Banchs, A. and Costa-P{\'e}rez, X.
entries.title: DeepCog: Cognitive Network Management in Sliced 5G Networks with Deep Learning
entries.problem: Per-slice capacity forecasting with asymmetric cost.

entries.relevance: Asymmetric SLA cost; inspiration for the collateral-loss design in C1 and for C6.

entries.authors: Salvat, J. X. and Zanzi, L. and Garcia-Saavedra, A. and Sciancalepore, V. and Costa-P{\'e}rez, X.
entries.title: Overbooking Network Slices through Yield-Driven End-to-End Orchestration

entries.limitations: [I] Overbooking increases the cross-slice coupling that magnifies collateral damage.
entries.relevance: Motivates the shared-resource coupling in C1.

entries.authors: Polese, M. and Bonati, L. and D'Oro, S. and Basagni, S. and Melodia, T.
entries.title: Understanding O-RAN: Architecture, Interfaces, Algorithms, Security, and Research Challenges
entries.contribution: Tutorial and survey.
entries.relevance: Background for C5, C7, C8.
